metadata.title: On weight initialization in deep neural networks

extraction_notes.note: The informal proof of Proposition 1 ends with \qedsymbol and no period, so the finishing step flags it as ending mid-sentence; the span is the author's full argument.

Label eq:tanh1 is defined twice (for v ~ 1/sqrt(N) and for the tanh pdf); the figure caption's \ref to it means the pdf (EP16). Also \enum{seq1} sits outside its equation, so eq:seq1 attaches to a section heading.
The text says the 30-layer network converges and the 22-layer one does not, which reverses the earlier description; the statement is copied as written.
Definition or claim: the sentence asserts equal moments by symmetry, but its main role is introducing $\mu_m$ and $s_m^2$.
The main results (general initialization formula, re-derived He initialization) are numbered equations that the text never names as results, so they stay equation nodes.
Single sentences introduce several symbols at once; a sentence can't be split, so each is one definition node with all symbols in definiendum.

Most of the argument is a chain of prose derivations linking numbered equations, with no proof environments. The equation-to-equation dependencies were added as uses edges by hand, and the connecting prose gets no node.
The CIFAR-10 experimental protocol (architecture, 10 training iterations, top-5 accuracy) is not an algorithm node; only its reported outcome is kept as a numerical claim.

nodes.statement: Since the RELU activation is not differentiable at 0, the results from (~--~) cannot be used to compute the optimal value of v^2. To proceed, I use proposition 2 and () which state that for the first iteration, y_m(i) sim calN(0,u_m^2). We are interested in in the mean and variance of x_m+1(i) = mboxmax(0,y_m(i)). The mean will be given by mu_m+1 = E(y_m(i)bfI(y_m(i)>0)) = frac1u_msqrt2piint_0^infty x mboxe^-fracx^22u_m^2dx = fracu_msqrt2piint_0^inftymboxe^-tdt = fracu_msqrt2pi. enumrelu1 Similarly, E(x_m+1(i)^2) = frac1u_msqrt2piint_0^infty x^2 mboxe^-fracx^22u_m^2dx = left(frac12right) frac1usqrt2pi int_-infty^infty x^2 mboxe^-fracx^22u^2dx = fracu_m^22. enumrelu2 Using () and (), s_m+1^2 = E(x_m+1(i)^2) - mu_m+1^2 = fracu_m^22 - fracu_m^22pi approx 0.34u_m^2. enumrelu3 For the variance to be maintained at each iteration, we require s_m+1^2 approx 1 which yields u_m^2 approx 3. enumrelu301 Plugging () in () yields mu_m+1 approx 0.7. By the symmetry of the problem during the first iteration, we expect mu_m+1 approx mu_m ... approx mu_2 approx 0.7. Using this result in () yields 3 = Nv^2(1+ 0.49) or v^2approx 2/N, which is consistent with that obtained by . subsubsection*To converge or not to converge, that is the question. In paper, the authors provide an example of a 22 layer neural network using RELU activations which converges with the itXavier Initialization, and a 30 layer neural network which does not converge with the same initializations and activation functions. To understand why this happens, I compute the central moments of x_m+1 in terms of the central moments of x_m when v^2 = 1/N. From () we have u_m^2 = s_m^2 + mu_m^2. enumr01 Plugging results from () into () yields the recursion mu_m+1^2 = frac12pi(s_m^2 + mu_m^2) approx 0.16(s_m^2 + mu_m^2). enumr02 Similarly, plugging results from () and () in () yields s_m+1^2 approx 0.34(s_m^2 + mu_m^2). enumrelu5 Simple manipulations of equations (~--~) gives mu_m^2 approx 0.16 times (0.51)^m-1 enumrelu603 and s_m^2 approx 0.34 times (0.51)^m-1. enumrelu602 for all m geq 1. These approximations are remarkably accurate, as is demonstrated by comparisons with the simulation experiments described in Figure . includegraphics[width=1textwidth]Figure3.png captionA comparison of the predicted means and standard errors obtained from (~--~) with the simulated values reported in slide 61 of . Equation () shows that the variance of the inputs to the deeper layers is exponentially smaller than the variance of the inputs to the shallower layer. Therefore, the deeper the neural network, the worse the performance of the itXavier Initialization will be. From (), s_22^2 approx 1.62 times 10^-7 and s_30^2 approx 6.33 times 10^-10. Thus the variance in the input to the 30^th layer will be (0.51)^8 = 3 times 10^-3 times smaller than the variance to the 22^nd layer, and explains the possible reason why the 30 layer neural network described in converges, but the 22 layer neural network does not. footnoteIt is surprising that the 22 layer neural network converges!
